(DRIs) for vitamin E are given in units of mg 2R-a-tocopherol (Table 1, see below for discussion). These same units are used for the
updated food and supplement labeling, where the daily value or “reference dietary intake” (RDI) is 15 mg (Food and Drug Admin-
istration, 2016). To indicate that synthetic a–tocopherol is a racemic mixture, it is called all-rac-a-tocopherol, or on supplement
labels, dl-a–tocopherol. Table 2 lists the factors to convert IU to mg 2R-a-tocopherol. For example, if a vitamin E supplement is
labeled 400 IU and it is dl-a-tocopheryl acetate, then 400 times 0.45 equals 180 mg 2Ratocopherol, but if it is labeled d-a-toco-
pheryl acetate, then 400 times 0.67 equals 268 mg 2Ratocopherol.
